messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on residential streets.
• “No speed limit” zones exist in some rural areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Guidelines | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield to emergency vehicles” when lights are flashing. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• “Lane‑change” violations can lead to points on your license. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Points System & License Suspension** | • Accumulating 4 or more points in 12 months can lead to license suspension.
• Points are assigned for various infractions (speeding, DUI, etc.). | Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) – Driver’s License Points | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and municipal regulations apply in cities. | City ordinances; Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – Vehicle Registration | | **Special Situations** | • “No‑stop” zones, “no‑passing” zones, and “no‑turn” zones are posted.
• Rural “no‑speed‑limit” zones require drivers to obey posted signs. | TxDOT – Roadway Signage Standards | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official website for driver’s license rules, penalties, and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. - **TxDOT** – Provides guidelines, signage standards, and roadway safety information. - **Local County or City Ordinances** – May have additional parking or speed limit rules. If you need specific details (e.g., penalties for a particular infraction, how to appeal a ticket, or the latest changes to the Texas Transportation Code), let me know!
